data.title: Why is AMD stock gaining today?
data.description:
AMD stock gained 2% on Tuesday after Piper Sandler reiterated its Overweight rating on Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and maintained a $600 price target.

The stock was trading at $504.62 and has risen more than 213% over the past year.

The rating followed AMD’s third-quarter pre-quiet-period call, during which management provided updates on its product pipeline and demand environment.

Piper Sandler sees strong demand across AMD’s portfolio

Piper Sandler analyst David O’Connor said the overall message from AMD’s investor relations team was reassuring, with ramp-ups across its central processing unit and graphics processing unit products remaining on track.

Demand continues to exceed available supply across AMD’s product portfolio, according to the analyst.

The discussion covered several areas, including the ramp-up of Helios servers, Venice CPUs, the Optics scale-up architecture, high-bandwidth memory supply, broader memory dynamics, margins, and the company’s client and gaming businesses.

O’Connor said the relevant programmes were progressing as planned, with supply in place to support AMD’s guidance and potentially exceed expectations.

He described the tone of the discussion as positive, adding that the business was operating at full speed as demand continued to outpace supply.

Piper Sandler views AMD as a key investment opportunity linked to the growth of agentic artificial intelligence.

The firm initiated coverage of AMD last week and published an in-depth thematic report on AI computing titled “Starving for Compute.”

Semiconductor demand remains strong

The broader semiconductor industry is also benefiting from strong demand, despite concerns about a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure investment.

Bank of America has forecast that the semiconductor industry’s total addressable market will nearly double from $1.7 trillion in 2026 to $3.2 trillion by 2030.

The bank expects growth to be driven mainly by memory and data centres, alongside an incremental recovery in the automotive and industrial sectors.

BofA analysts led by Vivek Arya said they had seen no signs of slowing customer orders, long-term agreements, capacity commitments or semiconductor pricing, despite rising concerns about AI infrastructure spending.

The analysts noted that recent DRAM and NAND memory pricing remained broadly flat week over week.

They also pointed to rising GPU rental prices as an indicator of continued demand.

Nvidia’s B200 GPU rental price was cited at $5.72 per hour, up consistently over the previous two months and less than 10% below its approximate $6.10 peak in March.

AMD has also indicated that it is not seeing signs of a slowdown in customer orders.

BofA identifies potential semiconductor leaders

Arya said 2027 remains largely fully booked or contracted across compute, networking and memory suppliers.

He added that 2028 could also remain constrained, driven by stronger demand for CPUs, XPU attachment, new optics-based scale-up technologies and AI accelerators from application-specific integrated circuit and GPU vendors.

Although the semiconductor sector could remain rangebound in the near term, BofA identified several companies that may show greater resilience.

The bank highlighted Nvidia and AMD in compute, Marvell in networking, and Analog Devices and onsemi in analog chips.

It also said Micron, Lam Research, Applied Materials and Intel could lead gains if market momentum returns.

data.title: Why is Alphabet (GOOG) stock falling today?
data.description:
Alphabet shares GOOGL fell about 1.7% on Tuesday as higher crude prices, elevated Treasury yields and renewed uncertainty over AI demand weighed on technology stocks.

The decline came as investors prepared for what is widely expected to be another Federal Reserve interest-rate increase.

Traders were pricing in a nearly 93% probability of a hike on Wednesday, while the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since 2007.

Other major technology stocks also came under pressure.

Amazon fell about 1.7%, while Microsoft declined roughly 1%.

The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF was down 0.8%.

The weakness came despite a recovery in semiconductor stocks following Monday's sharp selloff, suggesting investors remain selective about which parts of the AI trade they are willing to back.

Higher yields raise pressure on AI spending

The rise in Treasury yields is particularly important for technology companies because much of their valuation is based on earnings and revenue expected several years into the future.

Higher borrowing costs can make those future cash flows less valuable while increasing the cost of financing the enormous infrastructure investments required to develop and deploy AI.

The issue has become more pressing as major technology companies increasingly turn to debt markets to finance their AI build-outs.

Alphabet was reported last month to be seeking between $20 billion and $25 billion through a US bond offering, following a sharp selloff triggered by concerns around its 2026 capital spending outlook.

A regulatory filing showed that the company offered notes in as many as 10 parts, with maturities ranging from two to 40 years.

Alphabet is not alone in tapping debt markets.

Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle issued about $194 billion worth of bonds through July 7, up 79% from roughly $108 billion during the same period in 2025, according to a Reuters analysis of LSEG data.

At the same time, the hyperscalers are expected to spend more than $730 billion this year, primarily on AI.

The scale of that investment is already putting pressure on cash generation.

Alphabet reported its first-ever negative free cash flow in the second quarter in late July.

AI slowdown fears add another layer of uncertainty

Investors are also reassessing whether the extraordinary pace of AI investment can continue as industry leaders raise concerns about the technology's risks.

AI-linked stocks suffered a global selloff on Monday after leaders of major AI companies warned about potentially existential risks associated with the technology.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to slow the pace of model development in an essay posted on X on Saturday. Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman subsequently expressed agreement with Amodei.

Altman also said OpenAI would not proceed with an IPO this year, citing safety concerns.

The comments have raised questions about whether a slower pace of AI development could eventually translate into weaker infrastructure demand and lower capital spending.

However, some analysts see little evidence of an immediate slowdown.

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya wrote in a Tuesday note that despite concerns over AI investment, "we see no signs of slowing in customer orders, [long-term agreements], capacity commitments or semis pricing."

That suggests the fundamental demand behind the AI infrastructure buildout remains intact, even as investors become increasingly sensitive to the amount companies are spending to meet it.

Fundstrat sees Magnificent Seven breakout

Despite the near-term pressure on Big Tech, some technical analysts remain optimistic about the sector's prospects.

Fundstrat believes the Magnificent Seven basket of mega-cap technology stocks is approaching a breakout that could trigger a broader rally in large-cap technology, MarketWatch reported.

"MAGS is on the verge of breaking out and looks quite positive here, with stocks like Apple, Alphabet, and Meta having all firmed up nicely in recent days," said Fundstrat's Newton.

"These look more appealing than many semiconductor names, many of which have stabilized but whose rally has proven to be a work in progress - not dissimilar to what happened to software earlier this year," he added.

According to Newton, the ETF is close to moving above the 70.80 level reached on Sept. 3.

A break above that level could trigger a sharp rally in the Nasdaq 100 and large-cap technology stocks over the following weeks.

"While Nvidia and Amazon have both weakened ever so slightly in recent days, neither has shown sufficient technical deterioration to think these cannot rally back as the Magnificent [Seven] ETF breaks out - which I see as being imminent," he concluded.

For Alphabet, the competing forces leave investors balancing two very different narratives.

Rising yields and massive AI spending are creating concerns about financing costs and cash flow, while continued customer demand and the possibility of a Magnificent Seven breakout are keeping the bullish case alive.

data.title: Dan Niles admits 10-year could hit 6%: stay bullish on Meta stock
data.description:
Niles Investment Management founder Dan Niles says investors should prepare for stickier, higher interest rates, noting that the 10-year Treasury yield could realistically climb to as much as 6%.

Pointing to unprecedented peacetime deficit spending, huge national debt expansion, and intense corporate debt issuance from tech giants competing against the US government, Niles believes rate pressures are far from over.

Despite anticipating a 10% correction leading into the upcoming midterms, however, he remains strongly conviction-long on Meta Platforms (META), citing unlocked AI monetization channels and an attractive valuation relative to broader technology peers.

How Niles recommends playing US stocks

Facing a potential surge in 10-year yields, Dan Niles emphasizes three primary tactical rules: avoid fighting the Federal Reserve, do not fight the bond market, and respect what he called the historical market seasonality.

With the federal deficit hovering around 6% of GDP and national debt standing against the gross domestic product, structural pressures prevent monetary authorities from artificially suppressing long-term rates as aggressively as in previous cycles.

Plus, seasonal drawdown trends surrounding midterm elections historically drag stocks down by 10% between late July and early November – double the pullbacks seen in non-midterm years.

With the market continually pitching risky volatility against elevated valuations, Niles advised disciplined investors in a CNBC interview that they are under no obligation to swing at every pitch.

Why Niles is still bullish on META stock

While holding significant short positions across the broader market, Niles maintains an outright bullish stance on Meta Platforms.

Unlike mega-cap peers like Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, META previously faced skepticism regarding its ability to monetize massive AI capex without a traditional cloud infrastructure or API platform.

However, recent breakthroughs – including cost-effective open model deployments, expanded enterprise API integrations, and new AI agent rollouts across its 3.6 billion daily active users – have fundamentally altered that narrative.

Trading at about 17x projected earnings, Meta stock presents a valuation lower than the broader S&P 500 index and significantly cheaper than mega-cap competitors trading in the mid-to-high 20s.

Note that Wall Street analysts currently have a consensus Buy rating on Meta Platforms Inc.

Managing downside risks ahead of macro volatility

Looking ahead, Dan Niles cautions against ignoring broader market technicals, drawing parallels to previous market "AI speed bumps" where overextended equities underwent rapid, sharp drawdowns within weeks.

Although enterprise execution at companies like Meta offers compelling individual upside, macroeconomic headwinds – ranging from aggressive sovereign borrowing to persistent inflation pressures – continue to increase systemic risk across stocks.

Investors navigating this environment must weigh strong fundamental catalysts against a tightening macroeconomic backdrop.

Rather than chasing market momentum, the seasoned market strategist suggests maintaining cash reserves and tactical hedges until seasonal corrections clear the path for more favorable risk-reward entry points.

data.title: Qualcomm stock rises 3.9% as AWS deal boosts data center outlook
data.description:
Qualcomm (QCOM) stock rose 3.9% in trading after StoneX reiterated a Buy rating and $270 price target, highlighting the chipmaker’s expanding data center ambitions and growing exposure to hyperscale customers.

The investment case comes as Qualcomm seeks to diversify beyond its core handset business, where demand remains uneven.

Analysts pointed to the company’s agreement with Amazon Web Services as a key development supporting its longer-term data center strategy.

AWS deal supports Qualcomm’s data center expansion

Qualcomm announced its collaboration with AWS on September 8, under which the chipmaker will supply custom silicon and advanced optical connectivity solutions.

The agreement could generate up to $60 billion in payments over multiple generations and the next decade.

The deal includes 25 million warrants issued to Amazon at an exercise price of $161.26.

Of those, 3.75 million shares are already vesting, while the remaining warrants depend on Amazon meeting payment milestones.

Unlike some recent AI chip agreements involving customer warrants, Amazon would have to pay $4 billion to acquire all of the shares.

Qualcomm’s stock would also need to remain above the $161 exercise price for Amazon to benefit from the warrants.

Qualcomm has set a target of $5 billion in data center revenue by fiscal 2027 and more than $15 billion by fiscal 2029.

The AWS agreement provides a publicly identified hyperscaler customer as the company works towards those targets.

At the Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference, Qualcomm’s CFO said the fiscal 2027 revenue target remains at $5 billion, with Amazon orders expected to begin in the December quarter.

Qualcomm targets growth beyond handsets

Stone Fox Capital said Qualcomm is executing a major pivot from handsets toward AI data centers, highlighting the AWS agreement as an important part of that strategy.

The firm noted Qualcomm’s $15 billion data center revenue target for fiscal 2029, while non-handset sales are projected to reach $40 billion.

It also said the AWS agreement could accelerate Qualcomm’s data center revenue ramp.

The Stone Fox Capital analyst added that the stock trades at roughly 10 times its fiscal 2029 earnings target of $18 per share, arguing that the market may not fully reflect the potential of Qualcomm’s AI-related growth.

The diversification push is also taking place as Qualcomm faces the loss of business from Apple.

Apple is increasingly shifting its iPhone modem operations toward internally developed technology, which could eventually cost Qualcomm around $4 billion to $5 billion in handset revenue, according to Counterpoint Research.

MediaTek adds near-term smartphone competition

Qualcomm’s data center expansion comes as competition remains active in its core smartphone market.

Rival MediaTek launched its Dimensity 9600 Pro, described in the supplied analysis as the first 2nm smartphone chip to market.

The launch comes one week before Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 launch, scheduled for September 22–24.

The development adds pressure in the premium smartphone segment as Qualcomm prepares its next-generation mobile processor.

The post Qualcomm stock rises 3.9% as AWS deal boosts data center outlook appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Why is Vera Therapeutics stock reversing its premarket gains?
data.description:
Vera Therapeutics (VERA) shares ripped higher in premarket trading on September 15 as investors reacted to landmark clinical data.

The biopharmaceutical firm announced that its lead therapy TRUTAKNA (atacicept-vymj) met all primary and secondary endpoints in the final 104-week efficacy analysis of its Phase 3 ORIGIN 3 trial for primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN).

VERA’s study demonstrated a notable 76% risk reduction in kidney disease progression alongside true kidney function stabilization.

Including today’s decline, Vera Therapeutics stock is down more than 30% versus its year-to-date high.

Why Vera Therapeutics stock rallied earlier today

Tuesday’s explosive premarket rally in VERA shares was ignited by outstanding top-line findings from the 428-patient ORIGIN 3 trial, evaluating TRUTAKNA in adults with progressive IgA nephropathy – a severe autoimmune kidney disease that frequently leads to kidney failure.

Patients receiving the weekly autoinjector achieved an annualized eGFR (kidney function) slope decline of just -0.6 mL/min/1.73m² over two years, compared to a steep -5.6 mL/min/1.73m² annual drop in the placebo cohort.

Plus, zero patients in the TRUTAKNA group required long-term dialysis, kidney transplantation, or died from kidney-related causes.

Building on its accelerated FDA approval granted earlier this summer, Vera confirmed plans to submit a supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for full FDA approval in Q4 2026.

Why VERA shares pared back gains

Despite the stellar clinical outcomes, Vera Therapeutics shares quickly began giving up their early premarket gains as market hours approached.

Financial analysts point to a classic "sell the news" dynamic following a prolonged period of high market expectations.

Because TRUTAKNA had already secured accelerated FDA clearance in July and initial launch metrics were strong – with over 350 patient start forms generated in its first ten weeks – much of the ORIGIN 3 success was already priced into the stock's massive YTD run.

Additionally, valuation reality has stepped into focus: as a commercial-stage biotech scaling up operations, VERA reports zero prior product revenue and persistent net losses, alongside notable insider net selling ($8.3 million offloaded over the past 12 months), prompting short-term traders to lock in profits.

Should you buy Vera Therapeutics at the current price?

For long-term biotech investors, today’s intraday reversal presents a compelling structural entry point rather than a red flag.

Wall Street analysts remain decidedly bullish on Vera Therapeutics, maintaining a consensus "Buy" rating with an average 12-month price prediction of $77 – representing over 120% potential upside from its current trading range near $34.

The company boasts a robust balance sheet with a current liquidity ratio of nearly 10.9 and manageable debt, providing ample cash runway to support its commercial rollout.

While short-term trading may remain volatile as profit-taking settles, TRUTAKNA’s disease-modifying clinical profile positions Vera as a potential category leader in the multi-billion-dollar IgAN market ahead of its Q4 full FDA submission.

data.title: Evening digest: Clarity Act fails in Senate, US crude hits $106
data.description:
Crypto markets faced fresh pressure on Tuesday after the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act failed to secure enough Senate support to advance.

Bitcoin fell below $76,000, while rising oil prices added to inflation concerns ahead of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision.

Gold also declined as the stronger dollar and higher Treasury yields reduced demand for the non-yielding asset.

Clarity Act fails to advance in Senate

The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act failed to receive the 60 votes required to move forward in the US Senate on Tuesday.

Although the vote represented the furthest the legislation had progressed, the result was a setback for the crypto industry after years of lobbying and hundreds of millions of dollars in spending.

Negotiators from both parties had worked on more than 600 pages of compromise legislation.

However, disagreements over provisions including restrictions on senior government officials maintaining ties to crypto businesses proved difficult to resolve.

Republican Senator Cynthia Lummis made a final appeal before the vote but was unable to secure sufficient support.

The defeat could send the legislation back to the drawing board unless lawmakers find a way to revive the process before the congressional session ends.

The industry may now focus more heavily on the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which are developing regulatory initiatives for digital assets.

However, SEC Chairman Paul Atkins has warned that regulatory guidance and exemptions may not be durable without legislation supporting them.

Bitcoin falls ahead of Fed decision

Bitcoin fell as much as 4.9% from Monday’s high of nearly $80,000 after the Clarity Act vote failed.

The cryptocurrency traded around $75,960 on Tuesday afternoon, down 3.8% over 24 hours, after reaching an intraday low of $75,700.

Ethereum declined 3.9% to approximately $2,440.

Bitcoin also remained under pressure ahead of Wednesday’s Federal Reserve decision.

The CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed a 92% probability of a quarter-point rate increase, up from 59.4% a week earlier and 33.1% a month earlier.

A quarter-point increase would lift the Fed’s target range from 3.50%-3.75% to 3.75%-4%.

However, Bitmine Immersion Technologies Chairman Tom Lee and MNFund founder Michael van de Poppe argued that a hike was unlikely.

Van de Poppe said markets could remain volatile as the Clarity Act vote and Federal Open Market Committee meeting overlap.

He added that he would consider buying further declines and said Bitcoin could target $90,000-$92,000 if it reclaims $78,000.

Oil prices rise as supply risks intensify

Oil prices climbed after Saudi Arabia reportedly cancelled some shipments following the closure of a key export pipeline after drone attacks.

West Texas Intermediate gained 4.2% to $105.61 a barrel, after hitting $106.75 earlier in the session, its highest price since May 19.

Brent crude futures rose 2.4% to $108.30. Prices have gained more than 20% this month as fighting in the Persian Gulf intensified.

Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia had informed European customers that some September crude deliveries were cancelled.

Riyadh described the pipeline shutdown as a precautionary measure, while Energy Secretary Chris Wright said he expected operations to resume within days.

The pipeline can transport up to 7 million barrels per day and has been used to redirect exports towards the Red Sea as the US and Iran contest control of the Strait of Hormuz.

Goldman Sachs strategist Yulia Zhestkova Grigsby said the attacks on oil infrastructure increased the probability of Brent crude rising above $120.

Gold slips as yields and dollar strengthen

Spot gold was almost unchanged at $4,302 an ounce, while US gold futures settled 0.2% lower at $4,339.95.

StoneX strategist Daniel Pavilonis said higher energy prices could fuel inflation and increase expectations for higher interest rates, creating further pressure on gold.

The US dollar strengthened, making gold more expensive for overseas buyers, while 10-year Treasury yields reached their highest level since 2007.

Higher yields also reduce the appeal of gold because the metal does not generate income.

ING analysts said much of the hawkish Federal Reserve risk appeared to be priced in, but warned that gold could remain vulnerable if policymakers signal that interest rates will stay higher for longer.

The post Evening digest: Clarity Act fails in Senate, US crude hits $106 appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Why SpaceX stock is down around 3% on Tuesday
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) stock slipped nearly 3% early Tuesday, extending a roughly 2% decline on Monday.

Shares were trading around $144, close to the level of their $150 debut price.

The stock has nevertheless recovered significantly over the past several weeks after falling to a record low of $104.83 on August 3.

The latest pullback comes as investors look ahead to both additional lockup releases and a potentially important Starship test later this month.

SpaceX faces billions in upcoming unlocks

Unlike a typical IPO, SpaceX did not establish a single 180-day lockup expiration.

Its prospectus instead spread insider selling eligibility across roughly a dozen dates, limiting the amount of new supply released at any one time.

The staggered structure, however, has not eliminated the pressure from potential selling.

Shares fell around 3% during the latest major release after up to 319 million Class A shares became eligible for trading, representing roughly $49 billion at recent prices.

Another 59.1 million affiliate shares became unlocked the following day.

Several additional unlocks are scheduled before the end of 2026.

On September 24, around 320 million shares are expected to become eligible for trading.

Another roughly 320 million shares are scheduled for October 9 and October 24.

The largest release is expected two full trading days after SpaceX reports third-quarter results, which are expected in late October or early November.

Up to 1.3 billion shares, or about 28% of the relevant share pool, could become sellable at that point.

December 8 marks the 180-day expiration, when the remaining non-Musk insider float becomes eligible.

By the end of 2026, roughly 4.9 billion SpaceX shares are expected to have become available for trading.

That creates a persistent overhang for investors, particularly as early shareholders gain more opportunities to take profits following SpaceX’s recovery from its August low.

Starship Flight 14 approaches

While the lockup schedule represents a supply-side risk for SPCX, Starship remains one of the company’s biggest potential long-term catalysts.

SpaceX is scheduled to launch its 14th Starship test flight on September 22 from Starbase, Texas, according to the FAA’s Current Operations Plan Advisory.

September 23 is listed as a backup date.

The launch comes after CFO Bret Johnsen said last week that Flight 14 will be the first revenue-generating flight for Starship.

The spacecraft is expected to carry production-grade Version 3 Starlink satellites into orbit, which Johnsen described as a major milestone.

Elon Musk said Monday that Flight 14 will be the final test before SpaceX attempts to catch the Starship spacecraft with its launch tower.

“We've got flight 14 coming up, of Starship, and this will be the last flight before we attempt to catch the ship,” Musk said at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles. “So if this flight goes well, then on flight 15 we will try to catch the ship.”

Musk also said SpaceX could later this year, or more likely early next year, attempt to refly both the Starship spacecraft and booster.

SpaceX has already demonstrated the ability to reuse its boosters, but it has yet to successfully perform a tower catch of the Starship spacecraft or fly the ship again.

Starship is central to the valuation

The upcoming tests matter because a large part of SpaceX’s long-term growth potential depends on turning Starship into a reusable, high-frequency launch system.

Pivotal Research Group analyst Jeffrey Wlodarczak said earlier this month that achieving full reusability is central to whether SpaceX’s roughly $2 trillion valuation can be justified.

His $220 price target assumes Starship can achieve 20 to 50 flights per vehicle, low refurbishment costs and rapid turnaround times.

“Our $220 target is a call on reuse of 20-50 flights per vehicle, cheap refurb, fast turnaround,” Wlodarczak said. “If that is solved, the rest of the model can happen. If it is not, SPCX is a different and much smaller company.”

The potential scale is significant. SpaceX says Starship can carry more than 100 metric tons of payload, more than four times the capacity of its Falcon 9.

data.title: Tilray stock has slumped 55% this year: is it a golden opportunity to buy?
data.description:
Tilray Brands stock has remained under pressure and is underperforming the market this year. TLRY was trading at $4.15 after falling by 55% since January and by 62% in the last 12 months. Still, a contrarian case can be made despite its ongoing challenges. 

Tilray Brands is doing fairly well despite challenges

The cannabis industry is going through a tough situation, with demand falling, competition rising, and the rescheduling taking longer than expected. 

Tilray Brands’ business has been affected by these developments. Nonetheless, a closer look at its recent results shows that its business is doing relatively well. 

The most recent results shows that its annual revenue rose by 11% to $915 million in the last financial year. It rose by 25% in the fourth quarter to $281 million, partly because of its acquisitions.

Its cannabis revenue rose by 5% to $71.5 million, with its gross margin remaining unchanged at 44%. The beverage business generated $105 million in revenue, up sharply from the $65.6 million it made last year. Also, its annual revenue rose by 6% to over $254 million. 

The distribution revenue rose by 15% to $85 million, while the smaller wellness revenue rose by 16% to $19.7 million. These numbers mean that the company is seeing modest growth across the board, which the management has pledged to accelerate. 

The company also narrowed its losses during the quarter. It reported a non-cash loss of $37.9 million, mostly because of non-cash charges. 

Analysts are optimistic that Tilray Brands' revenue will continue growing in the foreseeable future. The average estimate among analysts is that its annual revenue will rise by 22% to $1.12 billion. It will then hit $1.18 billion next year. In most cases, Tilray Brands tends to outperform its top-line numbers, meaning that its real figures will be better than expected.

Another potential catalyst is the rescheduling of cannabis. Tilray does not have cannabis operations in the US, meaning that it may enter the country once the rescheduling process ends. The company said:

“Following recent U.S. rescheduling developments, Tilray continues to evaluate multiple pathways to participation in an emerging federally compliant, science-driven medical cannabis market.”

Tilray stock price technical analysis

TLRY stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the TLRY stock has been in a strong sell-off since last year. It has formed a descending channel and remained below all moving average indicators. 

The stock is hovering near the key support level of $3.69, which is part of a double-bottom pattern whose neckline is at $4.95. Therefore, the stock will likely retreat to the key support of $3.70 and then bounce back. 

If this happens, the initial target will be at $4.95. A move above that level will point to more gains, potentially to $5. This view will remain as long as it is above the double-bottom of $3.70.

data.title: Coinbase stock on edge as CLARITY Act odds of passing dip despite Trump concessions
data.description:
Coinbase stock jumped by nearly 10% on Monday after President Donald Trump made a major concession on the CLARITY Act and as Bitcoin and other tokens held steady. COIN jumped to $191.50, up by over 37% from its lowest level this year. 

Coinbase stock jumps after CLARITY Act concession

COIN stock jumped by nearly 10% on Monday after President Trump made some major concessions on the CLARITY Act. The new agreement allows for state attorneys general to take enforcement action on violations of the law, not just the Justice Department.

Another key concession is that the bill would require government officials to divest any significant financial interest in an entity that issues cryptocurrencies. This provision became of significant importance after Trump reported that he made over $2 billion last year from his crypto holdings. 

Trump is a major player in the crypto industry. He launched the TRUMP meme coin last year, with thousands of people losing a fortune as its price plunged. Trump also launched World Liberty Financial, which operates the USD1 stablecoin. World Liberty recently received a provisional bank charter from the OCC. 

Trump Media is also a big holder of Bitcoin, while his sons have large stakes in companies in the crypto industry, including American Bitcoin. 

The CLARITY Act would benefit a company like Coinbase because of its strong presence across various industries. It is the biggest exchange in the United States. It is also a top custodian of crypto ETFs and a major player in the stablecoin industry through its partnership with Circle. 

The act will transfer most of the regulatory authority from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to the smaller Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). Coinbase has been at odds with the SEC in the past. 

Still, despite the recent concessions by Trump, traders on Polymarket believe that the bill will not become law this year. Odds of the bill being passed have dropped to 19% from the year-to-date high from nearly 80%. 

Coinbase’s business is on a transition

COIN stock remains in a tight range as the company remains in a transition from being merely a crypto company into a platform to trade all assets. It has already used real-world asset (RWA) tokenization technology to offer stocks, commodities, and ETFs. 

The company has also become an important player in the predictions market through a partnership with Kalshi. These initiatives aim at helping the company offset the seasonality of the crypto industry. 

This transition explains why analysts have started upgrading the company. Compass Point hiked the rating from sell to neutral, with the target from $130 to $177. Morgan Stanley initiated the stock with a target of $250, while Goldman Sachs hiked its rating from $196 to $219. 

Coinbase stock is also benefiting from the resilience of the crypto market. Bitcoin remains above $78,000, while the crypto market cap jumped to over $2.6 trillion.

Coinbase stock technical analysis

COIN stock chart | Source: TradingView

Technicals suggest that the COIN stock has more upside to go. It has formed a bullish flag pattern, which normally leads to more upside over time. 

The stock has moved above the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA). It is also slightly above $181, its highest level on July 21. Therefore, these technicals point to more gains, which will be confirmed if it moves above the key resistance at $193, the upper side of the horizontal channel.

data.title: Crypto stocks slide as Bitcoin drops ahead of Clarity Act vote and Fed decision
data.description:
Crypto-linked stocks fell sharply Tuesday morning as Bitcoin declined and investors awaited a critical Senate vote on crypto regulation, with the Federal Reserve’s rate decision also due Wednesday.

Coinbase Global shares fell 7% to $178.

Strategy, formerly known as MicroStrategy, slid 5% to $130.32.

MARA Holdings dropped a more modest 2% to $11.2.

Bitcoin was down 3.1% over the past 24 hours, trading at $76,180.

The Senate vote is the day’s key catalyst

The Senate is scheduled to vote at 2:15 PM ET on whether to advance the Clarity Act, legislation intended to create a clearer federal framework for digital assets.

The bill needs 60 votes to clear the procedural hurdle, and its path remains uncertain given continued political disagreement.

Even if the vote passes, it would not enact the bill into law; it would only allow the legislation to advance in the Senate.

A failed vote could leave the industry’s regulatory questions unresolved for longer.

Why the stocks are falling harder than Bitcoin itself

The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, which tracks Bitcoin directly, fell 3% to $43.19, roughly in line with Bitcoin’s own decline.

But Strategy and Coinbase fell by wider margins, 5% and 7% respectively, than Bitcoin’s 3% drop.

Strategy’s business is built around its large Bitcoin holdings, which tends to amplify the stock’s moves relative to Bitcoin’s own price swings.

MARA Holdings also carries Bitcoin exposure through its mining operations and holdings, though its decline was more contained than Coinbase’s or Strategy’s.

The broader market fared better as the S&P 500 index fell only 0.5%, showing that crypto-linked names witnessed a stronger bout of selling. 

Ark Invest trims Coinbase

Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest sold shares of Coinbase, Circle Internet Group, Bullish, Bitmine Immersion Technologies and its own spot Bitcoin ETF on Monday, as crypto-related stocks advanced.

According to the firm’s latest trade disclosure, Ark Invest sold 36,628 Coinbase (COIN) shares, worth about $7 million based on Monday’s closing price of $191.45. Coinbase shares gained 9.24% during the session.

Ark Invest also sold 142,350 shares of Circle Internet Group (CRCL) across two funds, valued at roughly $13.8 million. Circle shares closed 7.53% higher at $97.42.

What comes next

Coinbase, as one of the largest US cryptocurrency exchanges, stands to benefit most directly from a clearer regulatory framework, which could support more institutional participation in the sector.

Investors are now watching two things over the next two days: whether the Senate advances the Clarity Act this afternoon, and how the Federal Reserve’s rate decision Wednesday affects broader risk appetite.

Both outcomes are likely to move crypto-linked stocks more than the market overall.

Analysts framed Tuesday’s selloff as a near-term reaction rather than a verdict on crypto’s longer-term outlook.

If the Clarity Act eventually clears Congress and Bitcoin stabilizes, Coinbase, Strategy and MARA could all benefit from clearer rules and renewed institutional interest.

Investors holding crypto-linked stocks are generally advised to keep position sizes moderate given that volatility, rather than treat today’s price action as a signal to go all in either way.
